move: monospace T-minus timer counts down with seeded RGB-split slice glitches
how: On a dark HUD grid a 210px monospace timer counts 00:10.00 down to zero over D (2.5x speed) with corner labels, a frame counter and a progress bar. A deterministic burst schedule from fx.rng marks 2 to 6 frame glitch windows every 8 to 30 frames; during a burst the red and cyan copies (mix-blend screen) offset horizontally by 8 to 34px with clip-path insets, the base layer gets a horizontal polygon slice tear, translateX and skewX, the timer may invert, the label flips to ##ERR_SYNC and the stage jitters 6px. Between bursts a faint frame-keyed opacity flicker remains, and scanlines roll 1440px per loop (an integer number of 4px periods).
adapt: Change the start time and speed, the four HUD strings and the accent colours; keep the burst schedule seed and lengths, and the 2.5x count rate scaled to D.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the HUD, timer layers and bar; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap timeline with one {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) glitch/text logic. The jitter writes transform on .stage; target el instead, and scope all querySelectors to el.
caveats: the timer ends at 00:00.00 and starts at 00:10.00, so it does not loop
no GSAP in the original; the port wraps the seek in a tween
shakes the whole stage element, which must be the shot root in the port
